questions.a: Customer support software brings customer conversations from channels like email, chat, phone, social media and SMS into one place so your team can answer them. Most tools add ticket routing, automated replies to common questions, a self-service help center and reports on team performance. Many now include AI that drafts responses or resolves simple questions on its own.

questions.q: Does a restaurant need customer support software?
questions.a: A single small location can usually keep up with guest messages by hand. Once you run several locations or a franchise, questions and reviews arrive across many channels and stores, and fast, consistent replies get much harder. Software helps you see everything in one inbox and respond quickly wherever guests reach out.

questions.q: What's the difference between a helpdesk and a chatbot?
questions.a: A helpdesk organizes conversations into an inbox or tickets so your human team can assign, track and answer them. A chatbot answers common questions automatically, such as opening hours, menu questions or reservation availability, and hands the guest to a person when needed. Many platforms combine both, so the bot handles routine questions and your team takes the rest.

questions.q: How much does customer support software cost?
questions.a: Many helpdesks charge per agent or per seat each month, and several offer a free plan for small teams. Enterprise platforms and specialized sales chat tools usually cost much more, and some only share pricing on request. Count how many people will use the tool and which channels you need before comparing quotes.

questions.q: How do I choose customer support software for my business?
questions.a: Start with where your customers contact you and pick a tool that covers those channels in one inbox. Then check how well it fits your industry, since many popular helpdesks are built for SaaS or e-commerce workflows like order lookups and refunds. Integrations with your existing CRM or POS, ease of setup and AI features that cut repetitive work matter next.

questions.q: Which customer support tool is built for restaurants?
questions.a: Momos was built only for restaurants and helps enterprise brands scale customer support across their locations. Its AI agent, Alfie, reads guest emotion from the review wording, visit history and preferences, then writes an on-brand, personalized reply within minutes. It can also issue points, coupons and offers from your loyalty platform.
